prompt: Four cities reported these temperatures (°F): Anchorage $-12$, Buffalo $-5$, Chicago $-18$, Denver $4$. List them from **coldest to warmest** using just the **first letter** of each city, separated by commas (no spaces). Example: $A,B,C,D$.
hint: Colder means a lower number. Put all four temperatures on one number line and read them from left to right.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm-up: which is colder, $-3$ or $-10$? It is $-10$, even though its **absolute value** is bigger. Negative numbers reverse the usual size order.
Colder means a lower number. Put all four temperatures on one number line and read them from left to right.
Among the negatives, the one farthest from zero is the coldest, so compare $-18$, $-12$ and $-5$. The only positive temperature, $4$, must come last. Then swap each number for its city letter.
$-18 < -12 < -5 < 4$ gives Chicago, Anchorage, Buffalo, Denver, so the answer is $C,A,B,D$.

explanation: The coldest city has the lowest temperature, which is the number farthest **left** on a number line.
Place the temperatures on a number line: $-18$ is leftmost, then $-12$, then $-5$, and $4$ is to the right of $0$.
From least to greatest the temperatures are $-18, -12, -5, 4$, which belong to Chicago, Anchorage, Buffalo and Denver.
Using first letters, coldest to warmest is $C,A,B,D$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Watch the absolute-value trap
steps: $|-18| = 18$ and $|-5| = 5$. The number with the **bigger** absolute value is **smaller** (when both are negative).
So $-18 < -5$, NOT the other way around — even though $18 > 5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Inequality chain
steps: Cities in that order: Chicago, Anchorage, Buffalo, Denver.
